# Product Specification

<!-- SITE_DESCRIPTION: Classic 2D arcade Space Invaders game built with React, Vite, TypeScript and Canvas API — deployed on GitHub Pages -->

## 1. Vision
Build a classic 2D arcade Space Invaders game as a React+Vite+TypeScript single-page application. The player controls a cannon at the bottom of the screen and must destroy all aliens before they reach the cannon line. Deployed on GitHub Pages.

## 2. Users and Actors
- Player: Desktop user (keyboard controls) and mobile user (touch gestures)

## 3. Problems to Solve
- Provide an authentic arcade Space Invaders experience in the browser
- Support both desktop keyboard and mobile touch controls
- Responsive layout that adapts to any viewport size

## 4. Product Goals
- Faithful recreation of classic Space Invaders mechanics
- Responsive design — works on desktop and mobile
- Session-persistent best score via localStorage
- Zero external game framework dependency — pure Canvas API rendering

## 5. Out of Scope
- UFO bonus ship
- Multiple high scores or leaderboard
- HTML overlays — everything rendered via Canvas API (ctx)
- External game framework (no Phaser, no Pixi.js)

## 6. Business Concepts
- Game States: menu, playing, game over, victory
- Alien Wave: 5 rows x 11 columns grid of identical sprites
- Shields: 4 destructible barriers between cannon and aliens
- Scoring: points per alien destroyed, best score persistence
- Player Lives: 1 life — cannon hit = game over

## 7. Product Capabilities
- Alien wave formation with left/right movement and row-drop on boundary hit
- Player cannon movement (keyboard arrows / mobile swipe)
- Player missiles (upward) and alien missiles (downward, random fire)
- 4 destructible shields with progressive visual degradation (destroyed after 10 impacts)
- Score tracking and best score persistence (localStorage)
- Game state transitions: menu → playing → game over | victory → restart
- Configurable reload delay (default 0ms, max 5,000ms)

## 8. High-Level Workflows
1. Player opens app → sees menu screen
2. Player starts game → alien wave appears, cannon at bottom
3. Player moves cannon and fires missiles at aliens
4. Aliens move left/right, drop a row on boundary hit, fire random missiles
5. Shields absorb projectiles from both sides with progressive degradation
6. Player destroys all aliens → victory screen → option to restart
7. Alien missile hits cannon or aliens reach cannon line → game over screen → option to restart
8. Best score persists across sessions

## 9. Business Rules
- Alien grid: 5 rows x 11 columns, single sprite type
- Wave moves left/right; drops one row on boundary hit
- Shields absorb projectiles from both sides; destroyed after 10 impacts
- Player has 1 life — cannon hit = game over
- Best score persisted in localStorage
- Reload delay configurable: 0ms to 5,000ms (default 0ms)
- Wave width ≈ 70% of canvas width on all screen sizes

## 10. Success Criteria
- All aliens can be destroyed to trigger victory
- Game over triggers when cannon is hit or aliens reach cannon line
- Score increments correctly per alien destroyed
- Best score persists across browser sessions
- Game is playable on both desktop (keyboard) and mobile (touch)
- Canvas fills the content area with adaptive sizing

## 11. Open Questions
- None at this time — scope is well-defined from issue requirements.

=== FILE 1: us-001-game-canvas-state.md ===
Title: US-001 — Game Canvas & State Machine
Story: As a player, I want the game to render on a responsive canvas with clear game states, so that I can navigate between menu, gameplay, and end screens.
Expected Behavior:
- Canvas fills the content area using flex-grow pattern from the breakout scaffold
- Game renders in one of four states: menu, playing, game over, victory
- Menu screen shows game title and start prompt
- Game Over screen shows final score and restart prompt
- Victory screen shows final score and restart prompt
- All rendering done via Canvas API (ctx) — no HTML overlays
- Adaptive sizing: alien grid and cannon scale proportionally to viewport
Acceptance Criteria:
- Given the app loads, When no game is active, Then the menu screen is displayed on canvas
- Given the player starts a game, When in playing state, Then the game canvas shows cannon, aliens, and HUD
- Given all aliens are destroyed, When in victory state, Then the victory screen shows score and restart option
- Given the cannon is hit or aliens reach cannon line, When in game over state, Then the game over screen shows score and restart option
- Given the viewport changes, When resized, Then canvas elements scale proportionally

=== FILE 2: us-002-player-controls.md ===
Title: US-002 — Player Controls
Story: As a player, I want to move my cannon and fire missiles using keyboard or touch, so that I can play the game on desktop or mobile.
Expected Behavior:
- Desktop: Arrow keys move cannon left/right, Space fires missile
- Mobile: Swipe gestures move cannon, tap fires missile
- Mobile touch zones: fire zone (top 80%), movement zone (bottom 20%)
- Configurable reload delay (default 0ms, max 5,000ms) prevents rapid-fire spam
- Cannon movement constrained to canvas boundaries
Acceptance Criteria:
- Given desktop mode, When I press left/right arrow keys, Then the cannon moves left/right
- Given desktop mode, When I press space, Then a missile fires upward from the cannon
- Given mobile mode, When I swipe left/right in the movement zone, Then the cannon moves
- Given mobile mode, When I tap in the fire zone, Then a missile fires upward
- Given a reload delay is configured, When I fire, Then I cannot fire again until the delay expires
- Given the cannon is at canvas edge, When I try to move further, Then the cannon stays at the boundary

Title: US-003 — Alien Wave Formation
Story: As a player, I want to see an alien wave that moves predictably across the screen, so that I can aim and strategize my shots.
Expected Behavior:
- Alien formation: 5 rows x 11 columns of identical sprites

=== FILE 1: us-004-projectile-system.md ===
Title: US-004 — Projectile System & Collision
Story: As a player, I want missiles to travel in the correct direction and register hits accurately, so that combat feels responsive and fair.
Expected Behavior:
- Player missiles travel upward from cannon position
- Alien missiles travel downward from random alien positions
- Alien fire is random — not every alien fires every frame
- Collision detection: player missile hits alien → alien destroyed, score incremented
- Collision detection: alien missile hits cannon → game over
- Collision detection: missile hits shield → shield degradation
Acceptance Criteria:
- Given the player fires, When a missile is launched, Then it travels upward from the cannon
- Given an alien fires, When a missile is launched, Then it travels downward from a random alien position
- Given a player missile intersects an alien, When collision detected, Then the alien is removed and score increments
- Given an alien missile intersects the cannon, When collision detected, Then the game transitions to game over
- Given a missile intersects a shield, When collision detected, Then the shield absorbs the impact
Related Epic: [Epic 0 — Space Invaders MVP](epic-0-mvp/epic.md)
Related Slices: Leave placeholder comment.

=== FILE 2: us-005-shield-system.md ===
Title: US-005 — Destructible Shields
Story: As a player, I want destructible shields between my cannon and the aliens, so that I have temporary protection from incoming fire.
Expected Behavior:
- 4 shields positioned between cannon and alien wave
- Shields absorb projectiles from both sides (player and alien missiles)
- Progressive visual degradation with each impact
- Shield destroyed after 10 impacts
- Shield destruction is permanent for the current game session
Acceptance Criteria:
- Given the game starts, When in playing state, Then 4 shields are displayed between the cannon and alien wave
- Given a missile hits a shield, When impact occurs, Then the shield shows visual degradation
- Given a shield has absorbed 10 impacts, When the next impact occurs, Then the shield is destroyed and no longer renders
- Given a shield is destroyed, When subsequent missiles pass through its position, Then they are not absorbed
Related Epic: [Epic 0 — Space Invaders MVP](epic-0-mvp/epic.md)
Related Slices: Leave placeholder comment.

=== FILE 3: us-006-scoring-persistence.md ===
Title: US-006 — Scoring & Best Score Persistence
Story: As a player, I want to track my score and see my best score across sessions, so that I can measure my improvement.
Expected Behavior:
- Current score displayed top-left on canvas HUD
- Best score displayed top-right on canvas HUD
- Each alien destroyed increments the score
- Best score persisted in localStorage
- Best score updates when current score exceeds it
- Score displayed on Game Over and Victory end screens
Acceptance Criteria:
- Given the game is playing, When an alien is destroyed, Then the score increments and displays top-left
- Given the game is playing, When a new best score is achieved, Then the best score updates and displays top-right
- Given the player closes the browser, When they return, Then the best score is restored from localStorage
- Given the game ends, When Game Over or Victory screen displays, Then the final score is shown

Fill all sections:

## 1. Architecture Principles
- Canvas-first rendering: all game visuals via Canvas API (ctx), no HTML overlays
- Single-page application: React + Vite + TypeScript
- No external game framework (no Phaser, no Pixi.js)
- Responsive design: adaptive sizing based on viewport
- localStorage for best score persistence

## 2. System Overview
Space Invaders is a client-only SPA. The React app renders a full-screen canvas element. A game loop (requestAnimationFrame) drives state updates, rendering, and input processing. Game state is managed in React hooks with Canvas 2D rendering.

## 3. Architectural Style
- Component-based React architecture with Canvas rendering
- Game loop pattern: update → render cycle via requestAnimationFrame
- State machine for game states (menu, playing, game over, victory)
- Entity-component pattern for game objects (aliens, projectiles, shields, cannon)

## 4. Main Technical Boundaries
- React layer: UI shell, error boundary, theme toggle (from AppShell scaffold)
- Canvas layer: all game rendering via Canvas 2D context
- Input layer: keyboard event listeners + touch event handlers
- Storage layer: localStorage for best score

## 5. Key Components
- GameCanvas: main canvas component, manages game loop and rendering
- GameEngine: core game logic — state machine, entity management, collision detection
- InputHandler: keyboard and touch input processing
- EntityRenderer: Canvas drawing functions for cannon, aliens, projectiles, shields, HUD
- ScoreManager: score tracking and localStorage persistence

## 6. Key Interfaces
- GameEngine exposes: start(), update(deltaTime), render(ctx), getState(), restart()
- InputHandler exposes: onKeyDown(), onKeyUp(), onTouchStart(), onTouchMove(), onTouchEnd()
- ScoreManager exposes: getCurrentScore(), getBestScore(), incrementScore(), saveBestScore()

## 7. Data Architecture
- Game state: in-memory React state (useReducer or useState)
- Best score: localStorage key 'spaceinvaders:bestScore'
- No server-side data — fully client-side

## 8. Security Architecture
- No authentication, no server communication
- localStorage is same-origin only
- No user-generated content — no XSS risk from game data

## 9. Deployment Strategy
- GitHub Pages deployment via Vite build output
- Vite base path configured for sub-path deployment (import.meta.env.BASE_URL)
- Static assets only — no backend required

## 10. Observability Strategy
- Console logging for game events (dev mode)
- Error boundary for React-level error capture
- No analytics or telemetry in V1

## 11. Related C4 Views
- [System Context](../c4/system-context.md)
- [Containers](../c4/containers.md)

## 12. Related Implementation Slices
See [how/slices/](../slices/) for all implementation slices derived from this architecture.

## 13. Technical Constraints
- React 18+ with Vite 5+
- TypeScript strict mode
- Canvas 2D API only (no WebGL)
- No external game frameworks
- Responsive: wave width ≈ 70% of canvas width
- Reload delay: 0ms to 5,000ms configurable

## 14. Open Questions
- None at this time.

Goal: Implement bidirectional projectile system with collision detection and scoring.
Related Epics: [Epic 0 — Space Invaders MVP](epic-0-mvp/epic.md)
Related User Stories: [US-004 — Projectile System & Collision](us-004-projectile-system.md), [US-006 — Scoring & Best Score Persistence](us-006-scoring-persistence.md)

Data Changes: Projectile arrays (player missiles, alien missiles), score counter, alien alive status
Sequence Flow: Fire event → projectile created → GameEngine.update() moves projectiles → CollisionDetector checks intersections → hits resolved (alien destroyed, game over, shield impact) → ScoreManager updates → GameCanvas renders
Observability Impact: Console log collisions in dev mode
Tasks:
1. Define ProjectileEntity type with position, velocity, direction (up/down), owner (player/alien)
2. Implement player missile creation and upward movement
3. Implement alien missile creation (random alien selection) and downward movement
4. Create CollisionDetector with rectangle-based intersection checks
5. Implement collision: player missile vs alien → alien destroyed, score +1
6. Implement collision: alien missile vs cannon → game over state transition
7. Implement collision: projectile vs shield → delegate to shield system
8. Remove off-screen projectiles from active arrays
9. Wire ScoreManager to increment score on alien destruction
10. Verify collision detection is accurate and performant

=== SLICE 5: slice-5-shields/slice.md ===
Title: 'Slice 5 — Destructible Shields'
Goal: Implement 4 destructible shields with progressive visual degradation.
Related Epics: [Epic 0 — Space Invaders MVP](epic-0-mvp/epic.md)

Sequence Flow: Projectile hits shield → ShieldEntity.takeDamage() → health decremented → visual degradation updated → if health <= 0, shield destroyed → subsequent projectiles pass through

=== SLICE 6: slice-6-game-flow/slice.md ===
